shorts.hook: Scientists found a 36,000-year-old frozen bison. Then they cooked it.
shorts.title: Scientists Ate a 36,000-Year-Old Bison in a Stew
shorts.outro: The next fossil was not so friendly. The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: In 1984 a paleontologist put a piece of Blue Babe, an Ice Age bison killed by a lion, into a dinner stew, and Doug got a bowl.

shorts.hook: This 42,000-year-old foal still had liquid blood inside it.
shorts.title: This 42,000-Year-Old Foal Still Had Liquid Blood
shorts.outro: The fossils only get older and creepier. The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: Scientists drew liquid blood from a 42,000-year-old foal found in Siberia's Batagaika crater, and Doug parks on the wrong rim.

shorts.hook: This 506-million-year-old fossil still has its brain.
shorts.title: A Three-Eyed Predator Kept Its Brain for 506 Million Years
shorts.outro: What happens next is even worse. The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: Stanleycaris fossils from the Burgess Shale still show brain and nerves after 506 million years, and Doug goes to meet one.
